correctness.rationale: The derivative map Df(n)=f(n+1)-f(n) is an onto isometry from real Lip_0(Z) to bounded real two-sided sequences and exactly intertwines integer translations with the bilateral shift. On a real invariant plane, the restricted invertible shift is an isometry in both directions, hence semisimple with unimodular spectrum; its eigenspaces in scalar sequences each have dimension one. The only real cases are a conjugate rotation pair or the +1/-1 pair. Rational rotation orbit normals give an origin-symmetric regular polygon; irrational rotation orbit gives a disk. A positive-definite ellipse averaging argument proves the sharp global Banach–Mazur distance sec(pi/N). Exact phase differencing and uniform normal-gap bounds prove the arithmetic jump profile. All dimensions, boundary cases, and quotient duality are treated. The optional finite checker passed 54 comparisons; infinite statements rest on the proof, not on sampling.

value.rationale: Doucha’s integer-line example establishes finite dimensionality without identifying any of its Banach-space geometries. The natural smallest nontrivial invariant dimension is two; a complete description identifies exactly which norm geometries and quotient preduals occur, including all even polygon counts and Hilbert geometry, gives sharp distance from Hilbert space, and explains why rational rotation frequencies produce discontinuous coefficient norms despite parameter convergence. This resolves a motivated classification rather than an arbitrary finite computation; it does not assert novelty of elementary spectral or polygon lemmas.
